stack.name: Klow Blend
stack.positioning: Sold by research-peptide vendors as a single multi-peptide vial combining a copper peptide with two tissue-repair peptides and an anti-inflammatory tripeptide, marketed for recovery, wound healing, and skin/collagen support.
stack.rationale: GHK-Cu is included primarily for its collagen-synthesis and wound-healing signaling. BPC-157 and TB-500 are frequently combined with each other on their own (see the tb-500-bpc-157 research pairing) for proposed complementary tissue-repair mechanisms. KPV contributes anti-inflammatory tripeptide activity distinct from the other three. There are no controlled trials evaluating this four-peptide combination as a whole — the rationale here is inferred from each peptide's individual, largely preclinical mechanism, not from data on the blend itself.
stack.ratio_source_note: Multiple independent research-peptide vendors list an 80mg vial containing 50mg GHK-Cu, 10mg BPC-157, 10mg TB-500, and 10mg KPV (a 5:1:1:1 ratio by mass). This figure was consistent across every vendor listing checked; no manufacturer-published label or independent third-party lab panel breakdown of actual vial content was available to verify it independently.
caution_notes: Combined effects of these four peptides used together have not been studied — safety data exists only for each peptide individually, and mostly from preclinical/animal models.
BPC-157 and TB-500 are on the WADA Prohibited List at all times (S2); GHK-Cu and KPV are not FDA-approved for injectable use.
None of these four peptides has an FDA-approved human indication.
stack.disclaimer: For research and educational purposes only. This is not medical advice. This blend is not FDA-approved. Consult a licensed healthcare provider before using any peptide.

components.role: Copper peptide included for collagen-synthesis, wound-healing signaling, and skin/dermal support; the majority component by mass in this blend.
Proposed gastroprotective and angiogenic peptide via nitric-oxide pathway signaling; one of the most frequently stacked research peptides.
Proposed to promote cell migration and angiogenesis via actin sequestration (thymosin beta-4 fragment).
Anti-inflammatory tripeptide contributing local anti-inflammatory signaling distinct from the other three components' repair-focused mechanisms.
